name: Cerebral Sinovenous Thrombosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Cerebral Sinovenous Thrombosis

criteria.description: Radiological evidence of thrombosis in cerebral venous sinuses on MRI/MRV or CT venography
Presence of neurological symptoms consistent with increased intracranial pressure or focal deficits
Exclusion of alternative diagnoses explaining symptoms and imaging findings
Presence of known prothrombotic risk factors such as pregnancy, infection, or thrombophilia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Radiological confirmation of venous sinus thrombosis plus compatible clinical symptoms with exclusion of alternative diagnoses
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on neuroimaging; clinical presentation can be variable.

searchTerms: signs of increased brain pressure in eye

common.symptomName: Seizures of focal or generalized type
searchTerms: seizures affecting part or whole brain

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting related to intracranial hypertension
searchTerms: nausea caused by increased head pressure

common.symptomName: Altered level of consciousness ranging from confusion to coma
searchTerms: altered awareness ranging from drowsy to unresponsive

occasional.symptomName: Visual disturbances including diplopia and blurred vision

searchTerms: cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

rare.symptomName: Subarachnoid hemorrhage secondary to venous infarction
searchTerms: bleeding around brain from vein stroke
subarachnoid bleeding due to vein infarct

rare.symptomName: Coma due to extensive cerebral edema
searchTerms: severe brain swelling leading to coma

laboratory: Elevated D-dimer levels (supportive but not diagnostic)
Prothrombotic workup abnormalities (e.g., Factor V Leiden, Protein C/S deficiency)
Normal or mildly elevated inflammatory markers
imaging: MRI with MR venography showing absence of flow in cerebral venous sinuses
CT venography demonstrating filling defects in venous sinuses
Parenchymal changes including venous infarcts or hemorrhages
other: Lumbar puncture may show elevated opening pressure
Electroencephalogram may show focal slowing or epileptiform activity

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of venous sinus thrombosis on MRV/CTV
Blood in subarachnoid space on CT
No venous sinus thrombosis on imaging
No venous sinus thrombosis on imaging

redFlags: Rapidly worsening headache with neurological deterioration
Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as papilledema
New onset seizures in a patient with headache
references: Saposnik G, et al. Diagnosis and management of cerebral venous thrombosis: a statement for healthcare professionals from the American Heart Association/American Stroke Association. Stroke. 2011.
Ferro JM, et al. Cerebral venous thrombosis: an update. Curr Neurol Neurosci Rep. 2017.
